messages:
ryan: hey team — our embeddings endpoint is seeing big p95 spikes after ramp this morning. p50 ~40ms, p95 ~850ms. no errors, just slow. started ~09:12 UTC. payloads are tiny (single short strings).

support-liz: thanks — can you share a minimal request sample + the model name and any batching config you set? also any request ids in the response headers would help.

ryan: sample body we send: ```json
{"model":"embed-large-v2","input":["short text"]}
```
headers: Authorization: Bearer <redacted>, Content-Type: application/json. we didn't explicitly set a max_batch_size on client side. traffic: ~200 reqs/s concurrency burst. weird thing: embeddings length usually 1536 but occasionally shows 1535 in logs (maybe unrelated).

sara: 1535 dim sounds like a red flag for truncation but shouldn't by itself cause latency. two main suspects: dynamic batching coalescing into very large batches + routing to cold nodes (KV cache miss). can you run a quick curl with X-Request-ID so we can tie to server logs?

ryan: running quick test: ```bash
curl -s -D - -o /dev/null -H \"Authorization: Bearer $KEY\" -H \"X-Request-ID: embed-test-983\" -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \ 
  -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -d '{"model":"embed-large-v2","input":["a"]}'
```
response headers we got: ``Server: redwood; X-Request-ID: embed-test-983; X-Node: node-12``

deploy-bot: [automated] deploy completed: runtime/serve v2.14 -> v2.15 at 09:10 UTC (commit abc123).

jordan: fyi I see autoscaler + rolling deploy activity around 09:09-09:13. there was a 2m window where some serving pods were being drained and traffic was routed to a smaller pool (cold start on a subset). dynamic batching on that model had batch_timeout_ms=100 and no explicit max_batch_size set, so coalescing tried to fill big batches during the drain -> long waits for tail requests.

support-liz: to mitigate quickly: set a per-model max_batch_size (recommend 32) and reduce batch_timeout_ms to 25ms. also disable \"prefer_full\" batching policy if enabled (it waits to hit batch fullness). i'll apply a temporary routing tweak to avoid the drained nodes.

sara: adding note: dynamic batching + node draining = classic tail spike. Also check concurrency pattern: lots of tiny concurrent requests cause scheduler to wait to assemble batches. alternative quick fix: switch to the low-latency quantized variant (embed-large-v2-ql4) via model override in your requests to lower per-token time. quality may differ slightly.

ryan: updated client config to set max_batch_size=32 and batch_timeout_ms=25. re-ran load test: p95 dropped to ~90ms within 2 min. thanks.

support-liz: great — we'll keep the routing tweak for another hour while the deploy stabilizes. i've opened a follow-up ticket (SUP-4729) to investigate the occasional 1535-dim anomaly — that may be a downstream truncation in our response serializer, low priority but we'll track.

ryan: appreciated. marking this as resolved on our side :tada:.

support-liz: closing notes: root cause = concurrent rolling deploy + dynamic batching policy leading to oversized coalesced batches + batch_timeout too high. mitigation = set max_batch_size, lower batch_timeout_ms, consider model-variant for low-latency. follow-up ticket SUP-4729 for dim mismatch and long-term batching heuristics.
